# Identifying cell types using known markers

Since the genes are limited to the features selected in the panel, we need to check if the features we want to look at are part of the genelist. For this we can create a vector that stores all the gene names by looking at the rownames

```{r}
genelist <- rownames(xenium)
genelist
```

Using known markers we can check with plots like Violinplot or Featureplot, which cluster express these markers. 
For example we could check CD3, CD4, CD8 for T cells, CD19 and MS4A1 for B cells, VWF for endothelial cells or LAMP3 for dendritic cells. 
    
```{r}

VlnPlot(xenium, features = c("CD3D", "CD3E", "CD3G"), pt.size = 0)
VlnPlot(xenium, features = c("CD4", "CD8A", "CD8B"), pt.size = 0)
VlnPlot(xenium, features = c("VWF"), pt.size = 0)
VlnPlot(xenium, features = c("MS4A1", "CD19", "FCRL2", "CD79A"), pt.size = 0)
VlnPlot(xenium, features = "LAMP3", pt.size = 0) 

FeaturePlot(xenium, features = c("CD3D","CD4", "CD8A", "CD8B", "VWF", "MS4A1", "CD19", "LAMP3")) 
```

# Differential gene expression analysis 

This manual annotation can be quite tedious. Thus another approach is to find differential expressed genes in each cluster.FindAllMarkers is a function that are significantly more expressed in a cluster compared to all other clusters. Using these marker genes we can annotate our cell types more easily by using the too ACT (http://xteam.xbio.top/ACT/). THis web-based platform help to automatically assign cell types based on gene expression signatures. The tool uses a large reference database of known cell type markers from various public datasets. It is recommended to use the top 30 most expressed genes of a cluster as input.


```{r}
library(presto) #using this package, the FindAllMarkers function will work much faster

xenium.markers <- FindAllMarkers(xenium, 
                                 min.pct = 0.25, #at least 25% of cell must express gene in cluster
                                 logfc.threshold = 0.25) #only genes with logfoldchange of higher than 0,25 are considered

top30_markers <- xenium.markers %>% 
  filter(avg_log2FC > 0) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>% 
  top_n(n = 30, wt = avg_log2FC)

# Loop through each cluster and print the gene names for the ACT input
for (cluster_id in unique(top30_markers$cluster)) {
  # Extract gene names as a single comma-separated string
  cluster_genes <- top30_markers %>%
    filter(cluster == cluster_id) %>%
    pull(gene) %>%
    paste(collapse = ",")

  # Print in the desired format
  cat("cluster", cluster_id, ":", cluster_genes, "\n")
}

```

# Rename Clusters
after we know which cluster represents which cell type3 we can rename the clusters.

```{r renameClusters}
cell.types <- c("0" = "Progenitor",
              "1" = "Tcell.CD4",
              "2" = "Microglia",
              "3" = "Tcell.CD8",
              "4" = "Fibroblast1",
              "5" = "EndothelialCell",
              "6" = "Fibroblast2",
              "7" = "Bcell",
              "8" = "PlasmaCell",
              "9" = "MuellerCell",
              "10" = "myeloidDC",
              "11" = "plasmacytoidDC")

xenium_BroadCellTypes <- RenameIdents(xenium, cell.types)

dimplt1 <- DimPlot(xenium_BroadCellTypes, label = T, raster = FALSE)
ggsave(dimplt1, file = paste0(fig_dir,"3_BroadCellTypes", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)
```

```{r}
unique(Idents(xenium_BroadCellTypes))

# save cell types as factors
Idents(xenium_BroadCellTypes) <- factor(Idents(xenium_BroadCellTypes),
                                        levels = c("Tcell.CD4", "Tcell.CD8", "Bcell", "PlasmaCell", "myeloidDC", "plasmacytoidDC", "Microglia", "MuellerCell",  "Progenitor", "EndothelialCell",  "Fibroblast1", "Fibroblast2")) # be carefull to use exaclty the same names as you have assigned previously 

#safe annotations as metadata
xenium_BroadCellTypes$annotationRes0.3 <- as.character(Idents(xenium_BroadCellTypes)) 
saveRDS(xenium_BroadCellTypes, file = file.path(data_dir, "3_xenium_BroadCellTypes.RDS"))
```

# Compare how many cells are in each cluster

```{r}
data <- as.data.frame(table(xenium_BroadCellTypes$annotationRes0.3)) 
colnames(data) <- c("cell.type", "count")

ncells <- ggplot(data, aes(x= cell.type, y=count, fill= cell.type)) + 
  geom_col() +
  theme_classic() +
  geom_text(aes(label=count),
            position=position_dodge(width=0.9), vjust=-0.25) +
  ggtitle("Cells per cell type") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
ncells

ggsave(ncells, file = paste0(fig_dir,"3_CellsPerBroadCellTypes", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)

```

# To which Cell type do TLS cells belong?

```{r}
tls_cells <- WhichCells(xenium_BroadCellTypes, expression = tls.status == 1)
plt <- ImageDimPlot(xenium_BroadCellTypes, group.by = "annotationRes0.3",
                                         cells = tls_cells, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2)

ggsave(plt, file = paste0(fig_dir,"3_tlsStatusBroadCelltypes", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)

tls_cell_types <- xenium_BroadCellTypes$annotationRes0.3[tls_cells]
tls_cell_type_counts <- table(tls_cell_types)
tls_cell_type_df <- as.data.frame(tls_cell_type_counts)
colnames(tls_cell_type_df) <- c("Cell_Type", "Count")
gplot <- ggplot(tls_cell_type_df, aes(x = reorder(Cell_Type, -Count), y = Count, fill = Cell_Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Cell Type Contributions to TLS", x = "Cell Type", y = "Cell Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
print(gplot)
ggsave(gplot, file = paste0(fig_dir,"3_Barplot_TLScells_BroadCellTypes", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)
```



# Find out which genes are mostly expressed in TLS cells

```{r}
plt <- ImageFeaturePlot(xenium, features = c("tls.status"), size = 0.5, cols = c("white", "red"))
ggsave(plt, file = paste0(fig_dir,"3_tlsStatus", ".png"), width = 12, height=12)

# Extract gene expression for TLS+ cells
# Get TLS+ cells
tls_cells <- WhichCells(xenium, expression = tls.status == 1) 
ImageDimPlot(xenium, cells = tls_cells, size = 0.05, alpha = 0.5)

# Extract gene expression for TLS+ cells
tls_expr <- GetAssayData(xenium, assay = "Xenium", layer = "counts")[, tls_cells]

# Sum expression for each gene across all TLS+ cells
top_genes_tls <- rowSums(tls_expr)

# Sort genes by expression level (highest first)
top_genes_tls <- sort(top_genes_tls, decreasing = TRUE)

# Convert to a data frame for plotting
tls_gene_df <- data.frame(Gene = names(top_genes_tls), Expression = top_genes_tls)

# Select the top 20 most expressed genes
tls_gene_df_top20 <- head(tls_gene_df, 20)

# Create a bar plot
top_genes_tls <- ggplot(tls_gene_df_top20, aes(x = reorder(Gene, -Expression), y = Expression, fill = Gene)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_classic() +  # White background
  labs(title = "Top Expressed Genes in TLS Region", x = "Gene", y = "Expression Level") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),  # Rotate x-axis labels
        legend.position = "none")  # Remove legend

ggsave(top_genes_tls, file=paste0(fig_dir,"3_top_genes_tls",".png"), width = 12, height=12)
```

# Overlay TLS status with ImageDimPlot
```{r}
# Step 1: Extract base plot (cell type colors)
p <- ImageDimPlot(xenium_BroadCellTypes, size = 0.3)

# Step 2: Get metadata including TLS status
xenium_BroadCellTypes@meta.data$cell_id <- rownames(xenium_BroadCellTypes@meta.data)

# Step 3: Get spatial coordinates from image
coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(xenium_BroadCellTypes)  
coords$cell_id <- coords$cell
  
  
# Step 4: Join coords with TLS status
plot_df <- merge(coords, xenium_BroadCellTypes@meta.data[, c("tls.status", "cell_id")], by = "cell_id")

# Step 5: Subset TLS-positive cells
tls_df <- subset(plot_df, tls.status == 1)

# Step 6: Add TLS overlay (e.g., red border dots)
plt1 <- plt + 
  geom_point(data = tls_df, aes(x = y, y = x), 
             color = "white", fill = "white", alpha = 0.5, size = 0.1, shape = 16)
  

ggsave(plt1, file=paste0(fig_dir,"3_ImageDimPlot_TLSoverlay1",".png"), width = 12, height=12)

```
